title: Privileged Remote Access: what it is and where each question goes

prose.text: PRA is the clientless path for RDP, SSH and VNC; Browser Access is the clientless path for web applications. This subject walks the PRA area and sends each question to the subject that holds it.

steps.label: What are the parts?
steps.text: Portals, consoles, approvals, credentials, policies and application segments, and their limits: [[zpa.pra.components]].

steps.label: How do users get credentials?
steps.text: Credential types, pools and the credentials policy: [[zpa.pra.credentials]].

steps.label: What can users do in a session?
steps.text: File transfer, clipboard, recording and session sharing: [[zpa.pra.consoles-policy]].

steps.text: [[zpa.pra.app-segments]], with access policy and step-up in [[zpa.pra.access-policy]].

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: Whether the features exist outside PRA is open {{gap:absent-from-base-zpa}}. A comparison with standard ZPA access is open {{gap:alternatives-guidance}}, and so is a comparison with dedicated PAM products {{gap:pam-comparison}}.
SSH in ZIA is covered in [[zia.ssh-control]]; the web-application path is [[zpa.browser-access.requirements]].

definition.statement: Privileged Remote Access is a clientless remote desktop gateway that lets end users connect to servers, jump hosts, bastion hosts or desktops using RDP, SSH, VNC and RealVNC from a modern browser, without installing Zscaler Client Connector or any browser plugin.

quotes: Privileged Remote Access (PRA) is a clientless remote desktop gateway that enables end users to securely connect to servers, jump hosts and bastion hosts, or desktops
from the end user's modern browser without installing Zscaler Client Connector or any browser plugins.
Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), Secure Shell (SSH), Virtual Network Computing (VNC), and RealVNC

third-party-access.statement: PRA is meant to give third parties such as vendors, contractors and suppliers, IT administrators and remote employees controlled access to privileged servers and applications, for specific consoles and a specific time frame.

quotes: PRA allows you to provide third parties (vendors, contractors, suppliers), IT administrators, and remote employees controlled access to your privileged servers and applications.
Admins can set up specific end users for specific privileged consoles with policies for a specific time frame.

credential-options.statement: An admin can supply configured credentials for short-term end users, or prompt end users to enter their own credentials when they use a privileged console.

quotes: You can also choose to provide configured credentials for short-term end users, or prompt end users to enter their credentials when using a privileged console.

absent-from-base-zpa.title: Whether recording, approvals and credential pooling exist outside PRA
absent-from-base-zpa.detail: Open question zpa-57. The help pages describe session recording, privileged approvals and credential pools as PRA constructs, and the PRA segment resource uses its own SECURE_REMOTE_ACCESS application type. No captured source states that these features are unavailable on standard ZPA segments, so the negative is not established. A Zscaler statement, or a lab attempt to attach an approval or recording policy to a non-PRA segment, would resolve it.

alternatives-guidance.title: Choosing between standard ZPA access, Browser Access and PRA
alternatives-guidance.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Native RDP/SSH with ZCC installed, credentials known, no recording: Standard ZPA access - treat the target as an app segment, user RDPs with their own creds over ZPA." and "Emergency admin break-glass with oversight: PRA." The help describes PRA, not a comparison with standard ZPA access. The Browser Access side is claim zpa.browser-access.requirements:non-http-use-pra. A Zscaler design guide or support statement would resolve it.

pam-comparison.title: How PRA relates to dedicated privileged access management products
pam-comparison.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "PRA is not a full PAM replacement. It covers session brokering + credential pooling + recording, but lacks the credential-vaulting / rotation / secrets-management breadth of a dedicated PAM (CyberArk, HashiCorp Vault). Tenants with heavy PAM requirements typically pair PRA with an external PAM." No captured source describes PRA's limits against PAM products, vaulting or rotation. A Zscaler product statement would resolve it.
